Population increased in South Tyneside

The estimated population of South Tyneside in 2024 was 151,393 usual residents, a rise of 0.8% since 2023.

This meant that South Tyneside's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of South Tyneside increased by 2.3%.

Over this slightly longer period, South Tyneside was also among the areas that had a broadly average population increase, of local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of South Tyneside

The average (median) age fell to 42.9 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of South Tyneside has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
South Tyneside is an area that is classed as urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, South Tyneside's population of 151,393 usual residents was made up of:

  • 26,991 people aged 0 to 15 years, (17.8%)
  • 91,863 people aged 16 to 64 years, (60.7%)
  • 32,539 people aged 65 years and over, (21.5%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, South Tyneside has a slightly higher proportion of people aged 65 years and over (21.5% compared with 18.9% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In South Tyneside, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in South Tyneside
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for South Tyneside, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More deaths than births led to a fall in the population of 477 people (-0.3%). In total, there were 1,320 births and 1,797 deaths in South Tyneside.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) increased the population by 304 (0.2%). There were 4,719 people entering the area and 4,415 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in South Tyneside's population of 1,432 (1%) as a result of 1,684 people entering the area and 252 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for South Tyneside was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of South Tyneside in mid-2023 is 150,124.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 867 people and internal migration estimates were revised downwards by 13 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 854 people.
